entities.summary:
The Battle of the Ten Kings was a pivotal conflict that occurred in the Classical era of empires and foundational civilizations, approximately 1500 BCE. This battle marked a pivotal moment in the history of the Indo-Iranian world, where the ten kings of the Bharatas, led by Bharata, clashed with the ten kings of the Panchalas, led by Divodasa. The outcome of this battle would shape the destiny of the Indian subcontinent and have far-reaching consequences for the development of Vedic civilization.

The core events of the Battle of the Ten Kings involved a series of skirmishes and battles between the Bharatas and the Panchalas, with the latter emerging victorious. This conflict would produce the Vedic text, the Mahabharata, which would go on to become a cornerstone of Hindu literature and a testament to the rich cultural heritage of ancient India.

The legacy of the Battle of the Ten Kings can be seen in the lasting impact it had on the development of Vedic civilization. The battle would shape the social and cultural landscape of ancient India, influencing the development of Hinduism and the emergence of the Indian subcontinent as a major center of learning and culture.

As the great Indian sage, Adi Shankara, once said, 'The Battle of the Ten Kings was a turning point in the history of the Indian subcontinent, marking the beginning of a new era of cultural and intellectual flowering.'
